text: Record the OpenAI Build Week jury outcome and close the recursive experiment
description: After judging concludes, record the official result as external evidence. Success condition: a jury win/recognition validates the strong claim that Aimparency coordinated human intent and AI action toward the stated real-world idea. If not selected, preserve the result honestly, analyze which part of the chain underperformed (idea, implementation, design, impact, or communication), update the belief about Aimparency's effectiveness, and create the next improvement idea. Do not mark the parent done merely because the entry was submitted.

status.comment:
Outcome recorded: not selected (winners list verified on developers.openai.com). Awaiting Felix's acceptance.

Official result (checked 2026-10-15): OpenAI announced Build Week winners ~25 Aug 2026 (later than the planned 12 Aug), on https://developers.openai.com/blog/build-week-winners. 8 winners in 4 tracks; Developer Tools: 1st Echo Canvas (Kevin Yang), 2nd Sentinel (Malik Bashaar Javaid). Other tracks: Second Voice, AirBridge for Windows, veTriage, Pulse, Mechanica, Dấu. Aimparency is not on the page — not selected. No jury feedback is available, so which link of the chain underperformed cannot be attributed from evidence. Observable pattern only: the winners each show one concrete, immediately legible end-user benefit (speech for dysarthria, vet triage, 3D museum), while Aimparency's entry demonstrated infrastructure (intent→commit provenance) whose value shows up over longer work. Belief update: a provenance/coordination layer does not win on a 3-minute demo; its evidence has to come from a real user's outcome. That next step already exists in the graph (operator validation sprint fdd2059a, first paid pilot 032b8a47), so no new idea is created.
